key_insight: Hierarchical multipoint anchoring strengthens buried interfaces in inverted perovskite solar cells, improving efficiency and resistance to temperature-driven adhesion failure.
engineering_relevance: Engineering the transparent-conductive-oxide/SAM interface offers a route to more durable, high-efficiency perovskite photovoltaics.
method: Pretreat transparent conductive oxides with a homometallic halide to guide ordered self-assembled monolayer (SAM) formation.
Increase surface hydroxyl species to promote multipoint metal–oxygen coordination.
Use cooperative chloride-induced hydrogen bonding to reinforce anchoring against accumulated thermo-mechanical stress.
evidence_signal: Devices achieved 27.3% efficiency (26.9% certified) and retained 94% of initial efficiency after 400 temperature cycles from −40 to 85 °C under ISOS-T-3.
watch_item: The abstract does not establish scalability or durability under combined outdoor stressors beyond the reported thermal-cycling test.
paper_title: Hierarchical interfacial anchoring for durable perovskite solar cells
